# Appendix A5: Terminal Only {#sec-appendix-a5 .unnumbered}

This appendix assumes you've completed [Part 0](../chapters/chapter_00.qmd) —
Python installed, `.venv` created and active, packages installed via
`pip install -r requirements.txt`. No editor or notebook tool is
required at all; everything in this book can be followed with a
terminal and a plain text editor.

## Activate your environment

Every time you open a new terminal window to work on this book:

```bash
cd llm-ft-drilling-completions-book/book
source .venv/bin/activate          # Windows: .venv\Scripts\activate
```

**Expected result:** your prompt now starts with `(.venv)`.

## Edit a file

Any plain text editor works — `nano`, `vim`, `notepad`, or a GUI editor
that isn't a full IDE. For example:

```bash
nano code/chapter_01/load_local_model.py
```

## Run a chapter script

```bash
python code/chapter_01/load_local_model.py
```

Output prints directly to the terminal.

## Run the tests

```bash
pytest -v
```

## Render the book (optional)

Rendering the book itself (not just running its code) needs Quarto —
see Appendix A, Section 2:

```bash
quarto render
```

## Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Likely cause |
|---|---|
| `command not found: python` | Try `python3` instead — some systems only alias `python` after activating a virtual environment. |
| Script runs but prints nothing | Confirm you're running it from inside `book/`, not the repository root — chapter scripts assume that working directory for relative paths. |
